$$
{y}^{′}=xy+1,\,y(-1)=0
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the Runge-Kutta (RK4) Method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $Δx=1.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{1}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{2}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{3}^{′}\,$ | $Δy$ |

worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c
$$

the increment in $y$ using the Runge-Kutta (RK4) method with step size $Δx$ is computed as the weighted average of four sample slopes:

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{6}({y}^{′}+2{y}_{1}^{′}+2{y}_{2}^{′}+{y}_{3}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the initial point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{1}^{′}=f({x}_{1},{y}_{1})$ is the estimated slope at $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(x+\frac{1}{2}Δx,\,y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{′}\cdot Δx),$

- ${y}_{2}^{′}=f({x}_{2},{y}_{2})$ is the estimated slope at $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(x+\frac{1}{2}Δx,\,y+\frac{1}{2}{y}_{1}^{′}\cdot Δx),$

- ${y}_{3}^{′}=f({x}_{3},{y}_{3})$ is the estimated slope at $({x}_{3},{y}_{3})=(x+Δx,\,y+{y}_{2}^{′}\cdot Δx).$

All four sample slopes are already computed. So, we just need to find the increment on $y.$

We compute $Δy$ using the Runge-Kutta method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{6}({y}^{′}+2{y}_{1}^{′}+2{y}_{2}^{′}+{y}_{3}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(1+2\cdot \frac{3}{4}+2\cdot \frac{13}{16}+1)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{41}{8} \\  & =\frac{41}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{1}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{2}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{3}^{′}\,$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{13}{16}$ | $1$ | $\frac{41}{48}$ |

To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =-1+1 \\  & =0 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =0+\frac{41}{48} \\  & =\frac{41}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{1}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{2}^{′}\,$ | $\,{y}_{3}^{′}\,$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{13}{16}$ | $1$ | $\frac{41}{48}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{41}{48}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0)≈\frac{41}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem

y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c the increment in y using the Runge-Kutta (RK4) method with step size Δx is computed as the weighted average of four sample slopes: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx, where

  • y′=f(x,y) is the estimated slope at the initial point (x,y),

  • y1′=f(x1,y1) is the estimated slope at (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx),

  • y2′=f(x2,y2) is the estimated slope at (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx),

  • y3′=f(x3,y3) is the estimated slope at (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx).

All four sample slopes are already computed. So, we just need to find the increment on y.

We compute Δy using the Runge-Kutta method:

Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx=16(1+2⋅34+2⋅1316+1)⋅1=16⋅418=4148.

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
−1 0 1 34 1316 1 4148

To get the values of x and y in the next row, we add Δx to x and Δy to y, as follows:

xnew=x+Δx=−1+1=0ynew=y+Δy=0+4148=4148.

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
−1 0 1 34 1316 1 4148
0 4148

Finally, we have y(0)≈4148.
